content: This medication should be taken at evenly spaced intervals. The tablet and capsule forms of this drug may deliver different amounts of the active ingredient. It is crucial to continue taking this medication, along with other HIV medications, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less of this drug than directed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) even for a short time unless instructed by your doctor. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, stomach pain, dizziness, fatigue, weakness, changes in taste, or tingling/numbness around the mouth. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not fully understood. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking ritonavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, this medication may increase your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, nonprescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ritonavir interacts with many medications. It can slow down or speed up the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can influence how ritonavir is removed from your body, impacting its effectiveness. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, blood sugar) should be performed while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the capsules in the refrigerator, away from light, and do not freeze them. Capsules may also be stored at room temperature if needed, but discard them after 30 days if stored this way. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store medications in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
